content: The document provides guidelines for the use of biomarkers in the prevention, diagnosis, and risk stratification of heart failure (HF). It emphasizes the utility of B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal prohormone of BNP (NT-proBNP) in various clinical settings. Key recommendations include the measurement of BNP or NT-proBNP in patients presenting with dyspnea to support diagnosis and risk stratification of HF, and its role in establishing prognosis in hospitalized patients. The document also mentions that BNP and NT-proBNP can be used to help prevent HF onset in at-risk patients and to guide treatment management. The document discusses how obesity affects the levels of these biomarkers, potentially reducing diagnostic sensitivity.
